Theory of beta decay. Fermi's 1938 prize was for neutron-induced radioactivity, not this.
Theory of Brownian motion. Not part of the 1921 citation.
Bose-Einstein condensation prediction (with S.N. Bose, never a laureate). Not part of the 1921 citation.

edges.claim: Reines and Cowan sought and found the particle Pauli postulated in 1930 to save energy conservation in beta decay.
Fermi's beta-decay theory fixed the inverse-beta cross-section that set the scale of the reactor experiment.
Slow-neutron chain reactions led to fission reactors; the Savannah River reactor was the antineutrino source.
The 1962 Brookhaven experiment asked whether neutrinos from pion decay were the same as the beta-decay neutrinos detected in 1956. Prize order is inverted: 1988 came before 1995.
The neutrino beam is made of pi -> mu + nu decays; the pion and its decay chain were discovered with Powell's emulsion method.
Reactor detection showed neutrinos could be caught. Davis's chlorine method ran in parallel (his 1955 reactor test) and comes from Pontecorvo's proposal, so this is ancestry, not dependency.
No material dependency found. Davis and Kamiokande detected electron neutrinos; the muon neutrino result was not used. Kept only to show that this arrow in the proposed chain is weak.
Bahcall and Davis (1964) proposed solar-neutrino detection to verify the hypothesis of nuclear energy generation in stars, i.e. Bethe's 1938-39 fusion cycles.
Kamiokande was a water Cherenkov detector: photomultipliers record Cherenkov light from neutrino-produced charged particles.
The solar deficit found by Davis and confirmed by Kamiokande is the problem SNO resolved; Super-Kamiokande is Kamiokande's successor and Kajita was Koshiba's student.
Oscillation needs at least two flavours. Super-K's atmospheric result is a muon-neutrino disappearance measurement.
Atmospheric nu_mu oscillate mainly into nu_tau, the partner of Perl's tau lepton.
Super-Kamiokande (light water) and SNO (heavy water) are both Cherenkov detectors.
SNO's neutral-current measurement showed the total solar 8B neutrino flux matches the standard solar model built on stellar fusion theory.
IceCube records the Cherenkov light of neutrino-induced charged particles in a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice.
Koshiba's SN1987A detection opened neutrino astronomy beyond the Sun; IceCube extends it to TeV-PeV extragalactic sources.
IceCube's science case is the origin of cosmic rays: high-energy neutrinos are produced where cosmic rays are accelerated.
Reines detected the first natural (atmospheric) neutrinos in 1965 and was a founder of DUMAND, the deep-water neutrino telescope concept IceCube's ice approach replaced.
Oscillations over cosmic baselines set the expected flavour mix IceCube tests; the discovery itself did not depend on them.
IceCube's best-pointing channel uses muon tracks from nu_mu interactions; physics established in 1962, but not a material precondition.
Anderson found the positron in cloud-chamber photographs of cosmic rays.
The positron discovery was made in a magnetised Wilson cloud chamber.
The positron is Dirac's predicted anti-electron. Anderson did not set out to test Dirac; the identification followed.
The 1948 motivation is literally 'development of the Wilson cloud chamber method'.
Blackett and Occhialini's counter-triggered chamber confirmed the positron and showed pair production (1933).
The 1948 motivation cites discoveries in cosmic radiation.
The pion was found in emulsions exposed to cosmic rays at high altitude.
Powell's charged pion is the meson Yukawa predicted in 1935.
The antiproton search tested the extension of Dirac's theory to the proton.
Velocity-selecting Cherenkov counters were key to identifying antiprotons.
The Bevatron, built at Lawrence's Radiation Laboratory and sized to make antiprotons, descends from the cyclotron program.
The bubble chamber is the liquid counterpart of the cloud chamber's track-visualisation principle.
Alvarez's motivation names the hydrogen bubble chamber technique.
Resonance spectroscopy from bubble chambers supplied the multiplets Gell-Mann classified; the Omega-minus was found in a bubble chamber.
The 1990 motivation: deep inelastic scattering was 'of essential importance for the development of the quark model'.
Elastic electron-nucleon scattering at Stanford was extended to inelastic scattering at SLAC.
Asymptotic freedom was immediately applied to explain the scaling seen in SLAC deep inelastic data.
QCD is a gauge theory of Gell-Mann's quarks with colour.
Renormalisable non-abelian gauge theory, shown by 't Hooft and Veltman, is the framework in which the beta function was computed.
Renormalisable QED was the template for a gauge theory of weak interactions.
After parity violation, CP was proposed as the true symmetry; Cronin and Fitch found it is also violated.
Wigner introduced parity as a quantum-mechanical symmetry principle (1927); Lee and Yang questioned it for weak interactions.
Kobayashi and Maskawa explained CP violation observed in kaons by requiring a third quark family.
Perl's tau (1975) was the first third-generation particle, found independently of the KM prediction for quarks.
The tau was found with the SLAC-LBL Mark I detector at SPEAR, the ring and detector of Richter's J/psi discovery.
Charm was required by the GIM mechanism (Glashow, Iliopoulos, Maiani 1970) that extended electroweak theory to quarks; the J/psi confirmed it.
UA1/UA2 found the W and Z predicted by electroweak theory; the 1984 motivation names them.
The weak neutral current named in the 1979 motivation was confirmed in 1973 with accelerator neutrino beams (Gargamelle).
't Hooft and Veltman proved the electroweak gauge theory renormalisable, making it predictive.
Renormalisability allowed the precise W and Z mass predictions the CERN project targeted.
UA1's central detector was a drift chamber, a direct descendant of the multiwire proportional chamber.
Nambu's spontaneous symmetry breaking was developed by analogy with BCS superconductivity.
The BEH mechanism resolves the Nambu-Goldstone problem of spontaneous symmetry breaking in gauge theories.
Anderson showed in a superconductor context that gauge fields can acquire mass, anticipating the relativistic mechanism.
Weinberg's and Salam's electroweak models use the 1964 mass mechanism. Award inversion: 1979 before 2013.
't Hooft and Veltman proved renormalisable exactly the gauge theories whose masses come from the 1964 mechanism.
Becquerel's 1896 search for penetrating radiation from phosphorescent salts was prompted by Röntgen's X-rays.
The Curies' motivation names 'the radiation phenomena discovered by Professor Henri Becquerel'.
Chadwick's neutron experiment used polonium alpha sources on beryllium; polonium was discovered by the Curies.
Fermi's motivation is neutron irradiation; the neutron is the projectile.
Cyclotron and Cockcroft-Walton accelerator were developed in parallel (1931-32).
The collective model unified the shell model's particle motion with collective nuclear deformation.
Nuclear shells fill under the exclusion principle.
Fowler's nuclear astrophysics measured the stellar reactions whose cycles Bethe identified.
Laue's experiment showed X-rays are waves by diffracting them in crystals.
The Braggs turned Laue diffraction into crystal-structure analysis within a year.
Characteristic X-rays are a property of Röntgen radiation found by scattering studies.
Siegbahn's precision X-ray spectroscopy measured the characteristic lines Barkla discovered.
Compton measured the wavelength shift with a Bragg crystal spectrometer.
Electron diffraction was interpreted with Bragg's law on crystal lattices.
Neutron scattering uses the neutron as a probe of condensed matter.
Neutron diffraction applies Bragg crystallography with neutrons.
Shull's neutron diffraction on MnO (1949) gave the first direct proof of the antiferromagnetic order Néel predicted.
Planck's radiation law was built to interpolate between Wien's law and new infrared measurements.
Einstein's light quantum generalised Planck's energy quanta.
Einstein's 1905 paper explains Lenard's 1902 observation that photoelectron energy is independent of light intensity.
Millikan's 1916 measurements verified Einstein's photoelectric equation; the 1923 motivation names the photoelectric effect.
Millikan measured the charge of the electron identified by Thomson.
Bohr's atom applies the quantum of action to electron orbits.
The Franck-Hertz experiment is presented as confirmation of Bohr's discrete energy levels (the authors first misread it as ionisation).
The Compton effect showed light quanta carry momentum.
Raman described his effect as an optical analogue of the Compton effect.
Schrödinger's wave mechanics developed de Broglie's matter waves.
Electron diffraction confirmed the wave nature of electrons.
Matrix mechanics grew out of Bohr's atomic theory and correspondence principle.
Born's statistical interpretation is of Schrödinger's wavefunction.
The Chandrasekhar limit comes from electron degeneracy pressure, a consequence of the exclusion principle.
The resolving power of the electron microscope is set by the de Broglie wavelength; Ruska learned of it after starting.
Perrin's sedimentation and Brownian-motion measurements confirmed Einstein's 1905 theory.
Stark found the electric-field counterpart of the Zeeman effect.
Appleton's ionospheric layer explains long-range radio propagation demonstrated by Marconi.
Kamerlingh Onnes credited van der Waals' law of corresponding states with guiding helium liquefaction.
Rabi's resonance method is a molecular-beam method; Rabi had worked with Stern.
NMR in bulk matter extends Rabi's resonance principle from beams to condensed samples.
Kusch measured the electron moment with Rabi's molecular-beam magnetic resonance method.
The Lamb shift and Kusch's anomalous moment were deviations from Dirac theory.
Renormalised QED was built to compute the Lamb shift and the electron's anomalous moment.
Separated oscillatory fields improved Rabi's method; Ramsey was Rabi's student.
Microwave and molecular-beam resonance methods underlie the ammonia maser.
Laser spectroscopy is the application of the laser; Schawlow co-proposed the optical maser with Townes.
The frequency comb grew from laser precision spectroscopy; Hänsch was Schawlow's postdoc.
Glauber's coherence theory was motivated by the need to describe laser light quantum mechanically.
Laser cooling and trapping require tunable lasers.
Optical pumping and light shifts are the atomic physics behind sub-Doppler cooling; Cohen-Tannoudji came from Kastler's group.
Ashkin's radiation-pressure trapping (1970) preceded Chu's Bell Labs optical molasses and trap work, done with Ashkin. Award inversion: 1997 before 2018.
Optical tweezers trap with focused laser light.
BEC was reached by laser cooling followed by evaporative cooling.
The condensate was the state predicted by Bose and Einstein in 1924-25.
Wineland's single-ion control uses Penning/Paul traps; he was a postdoc with Dehmelt.
Ramsey interferometry is a core readout in both Haroche's cavity QED and Wineland's ion clocks.
Laser cooling of ions (Wineland 1978) developed alongside neutral-atom cooling.
Attosecond pulse generation is driven by intense femtosecond lasers amplified by chirped pulse amplification.
Isolated attosecond pulses need carrier-envelope phase control, developed with frequency-comb techniques.
High-harmonic generation is a strong-laser-field effect.
Aspect's sources used laser two-photon excitation; Zeilinger's used laser-pumped down-conversion.
Kao's 1966 analysis concerned fibres for laser-based optical communication.
Room-temperature heterostructure lasers made fibre communication practical.
Hulse and Taylor's binary pulsar came out of a pulsar survey; pulsars were found by Hewish's group.
The binary pulsar's orbital decay gave the first evidence for gravitational waves, the waves LIGO detected directly.
LIGO is a kilometre-scale Michelson interferometer.
LIGO uses stabilised high-power lasers.
Black-hole formation as a generic outcome of collapse underpins the binary black holes LIGO observed.
The compact object at the galactic centre is interpreted through black-hole theory.
A mass limit for degenerate stars implies further collapse; Penrose's theorem does not depend on it.
COBE measured the spectrum and anisotropy of the radiation Penzias and Wilson discovered.
The 2006 motivation names the 'blackbody form': COBE's FIRAS matched Planck's law to high precision.
Dicke, Peebles, Roll and Wilkinson's companion paper interpreted the excess noise as relic radiation.
Peebles' predictions of CMB anisotropy and its acoustic structure framed what COBE looked for.
Peebles argued for a cosmological constant in the 1980s; the supernova result found one.
CMB and supernovae are independent pillars of the same cosmological model.
Type Ia supernovae are standardisable because they are white dwarfs exploding near the Chandrasekhar mass.
The 2011 Nobel material states that CCD sensors (Nobel 2009) made the supernova searches possible.
The ELODIE radial-velocity spectrograph recorded spectra on a CCD.
The Holmdel horn receiver used a ruby travelling-wave maser amplifier.
BCS explained superconductivity, which Kamerlingh Onnes discovered in 1911 and described in his Nobel lecture.
Superfluidity was discovered in liquid helium, first produced by Kamerlingh Onnes.
Landau's two-fluid theory explained Kapitsa's superfluidity. Award inversion: 1962 before 1978.
Ginzburg-Landau theory (1950) is the base of Abrikosov's vortex lattice; Ginzburg shares the 2003 prize.
Leggett's theory of superfluid helium-3 is BCS-type pairing with spin-triplet order.
Leggett's theory explained the helium-3 phases Lee, Osheroff and Richardson observed.
Pairing in helium-3 was anticipated as a BCS analogue before its observation.
Giaever's tunnelling measured the superconducting energy gap predicted by BCS.
Josephson derived the supercurrent through a barrier within BCS pairing theory.
The 2025 circuit is a Josephson junction; the scientific background explicitly connects the work to the 1973 prize.
Leggett (1978) proposed macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits; with Caldeira he gave the dissipative theory the experiments tested.
High-Tc superconductivity extended the field beyond BCS's conventional range; pairing of electrons persists.
Esaki's tunnel diode came from heavily doped semiconductor junctions.
The STM exploits vacuum electron tunnelling; Binnig and Rohrer drew on tunnelling-junction work.
The integrated circuit integrates transistors on one chip.
Kroemer's 1957 heterojunction transistor proposal improved Shockley's transistor.
Efficient GaN blue LEDs use double-heterostructure and quantum-well designs.
The quantum Hall effect was found in silicon MOSFETs.
The fractional effect was found in high-mobility GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructures with modulation doping.
The fractional quantum Hall effect was discovered extending integer quantum Hall measurements.
TKNN's topological invariant explains the exact quantisation of the integer quantum Hall effect.
Topological order in fractional quantum Hall states is part of the topological-phases programme.
The anomalous quantum Hall effect in graphene (2005) was key evidence of its Dirac electrons.
Kosterlitz-Thouless and Wilson's renormalisation group were developed in parallel; RG later made KT quantitative.
Landau's mean-field theory of phase transitions is the starting point Wilson's RG corrects.
Landau-de Gennes theory extends Landau's order-parameter approach to liquid crystals.
GMR multilayers rely on antiferromagnetic interlayer coupling.
Mott's two-current model of spin-dependent conduction explains GMR.
Parisi solved the mean-field spin glass, the problem posed by the Edwards-Anderson model.
The Hopfield network's energy function is a spin-glass (Ising) Hamiltonian.
Replica methods from spin-glass theory were used to compute Hopfield-network capacity (1985).
